text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Finance Ministers at G7 meeting call for a halt to the dollar's surge.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe holds meeting on youth employment today.
-- Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur to reorganise French agro-food export promotion agencies.
-- Telecommunications and defence group Compagnie des Signaux to bid for a 64 percent stake in Cisi currently held by CEA-Industrie. Cap Gemini holds the remaining 36 percent in Cisi.
-- Shell oil group to downgrade its southern France Berre refinery capacity to 3.5 million tonnes a year from 6.0 million.
LA TRIBUNE
-- France Telecom seeks to buy 100 percent of ODA, a phone book company owned by Havas media group.
-- Belgian businessman Albert Frere to increase stake in Havas via Audiofina.
-- Blue-chip CAC 40 index reaches new record high.
-- Luxury goods firm Christian Dior to rehuffle its Japanese retail network to improve its image.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Rhone-Poulenc chairman Jean-Rene Fourtou in an interview says that Rhone-Poulenc seeks to increase profit per share by 20 percent in 1997 and 1998.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Air Inter Europe pilots hold one-day snap strike.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe in an interview says seeks to mobilise all sectors of the economy for youth employment.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- EU and Japan breathe easier but keep eyes fixed on dollar.
-- Jobs crisis in France and Germany imperils Europe's single currency agenda.
